title: Applying RICE, MoSCoW & Weighted Scoring
description: Practice using popular prioritization frameworks to make faster, more confident product and business decisions.

interactions.prompt: In the RICE scoring framework, the four factors are Reach, Impact, Confidence, and ____.

options.text: Effort
Efficiency
Expense
Engagement

interactions.prompt: A Shopify PM scores three features: Feature A (RICE: 120), Feature B (RICE: 85), Feature C (RICE: 200). Feature C has only 50% confidence. What's the key insight?

options.text: Feature C is clearly the best choice regardless
Feature A should be prioritized since it's most balanced
Feature C's low confidence means its true score may be much lower
Feature B should be eliminated immediately

interactions.prompt: You're a product lead at Slack. You can ship a 'Must Have' bug fix affecting 10% of users or a 'Should Have' feature requested by your largest enterprise client worth $2M ARR. Which do you prioritize?

options.text: Ship the bug fix — Must Haves always come first in MoSCoW
Ship the enterprise feature — revenue impact outweighs category labels
Do both simultaneously by splitting the team evenly
Delay both and gather more data first

interactions.prompt: Stripe's team calculates Cost of Delay: Project X loses $50K/week if delayed, takes 4 weeks. Project Y loses $30K/week if delayed, takes 1 week. Which metric matters most here?

options.text: Total cost of delay favors Project X
Cost of Delay Divided by Duration (CD3) favors Project Y
Both projects have equal urgency
Weekly delay cost is the only factor that matters

interactions.prompt: Using MoSCoW, rank these Airbnb feature requests from highest to lowest priority: (a) 'Nice to Have' dark mode theme, (b) 'Must Have' payment processing fix, (c) 'Won't Have' AR room tours, (d) 'Should Have' improved search filters.

options.text: Dark mode theme — Nice to Have
Payment processing fix — Must Have
AR room tours — Won't Have
Improved search filters — Should Have

interactions.prompt: You're using weighted scoring at HubSpot with criteria: Revenue Impact (40%), Customer Satisfaction (35%), Engineering Effort (25%). Feature A scores 8, 6, 3. Feature B scores 5, 9, 7. Which do you choose?

options.text: Feature A — higher revenue impact score wins with 40% weight
Feature B — its weighted total (7.10) beats Feature A (5.85)
They're essentially tied, flip a coin
Neither — scores below 8 weighted average shouldn't ship

interactions.prompt: Rank these four Notion features by ICE score (Impact × Confidence × Ease, each 1-10): (a) Impact 9, Confidence 4, Ease 3, (b) Impact 7, Confidence 8, Ease 7, (c) Impact 10, Confidence 3, Ease 2, (d) Impact 6, Confidence 9, Ease 8.

options.text: ICE = 108
ICE = 392
ICE = 60
ICE = 432

interactions.prompt: Your CEO just announced Notion is pivoting to focus on enterprise clients. The feature with ICE score 432 (Impact 6, Confidence 9, Ease 8) was designed for individual users. How does this change your priority?

options.text: Keep it top priority — the ICE score doesn't change
Drop its Impact score significantly since the target market shifted
Only adjust Confidence downward, keep Impact and Ease the same
Remove it entirely — individual user features are now irrelevant

interactions.priorContext: Previously you ranked four Notion features by ICE score. The top-ranked feature (ICE 432) targeted individual users. Now the company is pivoting to enterprise clients, changing strategic alignment.
